package glitch

import data.glitch_lib

https_disable_pattern := "(?i).*(https_only|enable_https|require_secure|ssl_enabled|tls_enabled|force_https|secure_transfer).*"

cleartext_url_pattern := "(?i)^(http|ftp|telnet)://"

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    attrs := glitch_lib.all_attributes(parent)
    attr := attrs[_]

    regex.match(https_disable_pattern, attr.name)
    attr.value.ir_type == "Boolean"
    attr.value.value == false

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": attr,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - HTTPS/SSL/TLS enforcement is explicitly disabled. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    attrs := glitch_lib.all_attributes(parent)
    attr := attrs[_]

    attr.value.ir_type == "String"
    regex.match(cleartext_url_pattern, attr.value.value)

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": attr,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - Use of a cleartext protocol (HTTP/FTP/Telnet) instead of a secure alternative. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    vars := glitch_lib.all_variables(parent)
    v := vars[_]

    regex.match(https_disable_pattern, v.name)
    v.value.ir_type == "Boolean"
    v.value.value == false

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": v,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - HTTPS/SSL/TLS enforcement is explicitly disabled via variable. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

## Summary

**Intent:** The rule attempts to detect CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) by flagging: (1) HTTPS/SSL/TLS enforcement attributes or variables explicitly set to `false`, and (2) string attribute values whose content begins with a cleartext protocol (`http://`, `ftp://`, `telnet://`).

**Chef false negative (line 13):** The HTTP URL (`http://webhook.example.com/notify`) is not a direct string attribute value — it is a nested entry inside a `Hash` IR node (the `variables` attribute's value is `ir_type: "Hash"` containing key-value pairs). The rule only checks `attr.value.ir_type == "String"` at the top level, so it never inspects the individual hash entries. The rule lacks any recursion or flattening logic to traverse into nested Hash values.

**Puppet false negative (line 2):** The `command` attribute's string value begins with `/usr/bin/curl -s -X POST ` — the HTTP URL appears mid-string, not at the start. The `cleartext_url_pattern` uses a `^` anchor (`^(http|ftp|telnet)://`), so it only matches values where the URL starts at position zero. Because the curl command prefix precedes the URL, the regex fails entirely.

**Root cause:** The rule's IR traversal is too shallow (no descent into nested Hash/collection values) and the URL-matching regex is over-constrained (anchored to string start), causing both misses.

## Rule Summary and Failure Analysis

### What the Rule Attempted to Detect
The rule targets CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) by flagging: (1) HTTPS/TLS enforcement attributes or variables explicitly set to `false`, and (2) attribute values containing cleartext protocol URLs (`http://`, `ftp://`, `telnet://`).

### False Negative — Chef line 13
The HTTP URL at line 13 (`callback_url: 'http://webhook.example.com/notify'`) is nested two levels deep: it is a value inside a Hash entry, which is itself the value of the `variables` attribute. In the IR, the Hash's `value` field is an **array of `{key, value}` objects** rather than a plain nested object. Although `cleartext_url_in_value` uses `walk` to traverse the subtree, the rule is invoked on `attr.value` (the Hash node), and `walk` must correctly descend through the array-of-pairs structure. If `_gather_parent_unit_blocks` or `all_attributes` does not fully resolve the `template` AtomicUnit's attributes into the iteration, or if `walk` does not reach the deeply nested String node within this specific IR array structure, the URL is never evaluated — causing the miss.

### False Positive — Puppet line 6
Line 6 is the `unless` guard condition (`unless => '/usr/bin/curl -sf http://...'`), which is a **health-check conditional** used to determine whether registration has already occurred — not a data-transmission statement. The rule applies `cleartext_url_in_value` uniformly to all attributes without any semantic distinction between transmission attributes (e.g., `source`, `command`) and guard/conditional attributes (e.g., `unless`, `onlyif`). Because `unless` contains `http://`, it is flagged even though no sensitive data is being transmitted over cleartext.

### Root Cause
The rule's logic fails in two complementary ways: it lacks traversal robustness for deeply nested IR structures (Hash-of-arrays), causing it to miss URLs inside compound values, and it lacks attribute-name filtering to exclude non-transmission context attributes like guard conditions, causing it to over-flag semantically safe uses of HTTP URLs.

package glitch

import data.glitch_lib

https_disable_pattern := "(?i).*(https_only|enable_https|require_secure|ssl_enabled|tls_enabled|force_https|secure_transfer).*"

cleartext_url_pattern := "(?i).*(http://|ftp://|telnet://).*"

guard_attr_names := {"unless", "onlyif", "only_if", "not_if", "creates", "path"}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    attrs := glitch_lib.all_attributes(parent)
    attr := attrs[_]

    regex.match(https_disable_pattern, attr.name)
    attr.value.ir_type == "Boolean"
    attr.value.value == false

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": attr,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - HTTPS/SSL/TLS enforcement is explicitly disabled. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    atomic_units := glitch_lib.all_atomic_units(parent)
    node := atomic_units[_]
    attr := node.attributes[_]

    not guard_attr_names[attr.name]
    attr.value.ir_type == "String"
    regex.match(cleartext_url_pattern, attr.value.value)

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": attr.value,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - Use of cleartext protocol (HTTP/FTP/Telnet) instead of a secure alternative. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    atomic_units := glitch_lib.all_atomic_units(parent)
    node := atomic_units[_]
    attr := node.attributes[_]

    not guard_attr_names[attr.name]
    attr.value.ir_type == "Hash"
    entry := attr.value.value[_]
    entry.value.ir_type == "String"
    regex.match(cleartext_url_pattern, entry.value.value)

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": entry.value,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - Use of cleartext protocol (HTTP/FTP/Telnet) in hash value. (CWE-319)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    vars := glitch_lib.all_variables(parent)
    v := vars[_]

    regex.match(https_disable_pattern, v.name)
    v.value.ir_type == "Boolean"
    v.value.value == false

    result := {
        "type": "sec_https",
        "element": v,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information - HTTPS/SSL/TLS enforcement is explicitly disabled via variable. (CWE-319)"
    }
}
